initial point and learning rate

bullets: May reach different minimum value based on:
X is in between -9.7 and color red bold -9.6

layout.arrangement: Title top-left; slide number in a yellow circle at the top-right; a small parameter box at the left-middle; the formula and explanatory annotation in the center; a function plot with a local-minimum callout at the right; a large numeric table across the bottom.

regions.name: Title block
regions.content: Red title 'Non-Convex Function' above a blue two-line subtitle.

regions.name: Parameter box
regions.content: Small bordered box with rows step/initial x/delta x and values 0.1/-11/0.1; a red block arrow points from it toward the table.

regions.name: Formula and annotation
regions.content: Fraction formula for f(x), then two annotation lines about the interval for X and f(x).

regions.name: Function plot
regions.content: Green oscillating curve, red initial point, orange arrow to a green square local minimum, purple 'Reach Local Minima' callout.

regions.name: Numeric table
regions.content: Eight labeled rows and sixteen data columns showing x, f(x), x-delta, f(x-delta), x+delta, f(x+delta), slope, and next x.

layout.hierarchy: The red title is largest; the blue subtitle is second; the dense table dominates the lower half visually; the plot is the main graphic; the formula and annotation are smaller center text; the parameter box is smallest.

visual_elements.position: bottom center/right, spanning most of the slide width

visual_elements.description: Cartesian plot of the same non-convex function. Horizontal axis labeled x with ticks -12, -10, -8, -6, -4, -2; vertical axis labeled y with ticks 0, -2, -4, -6, -8, -10 and space above 0 for the initial point. A green curve oscillates through several local minima/maxima. A red/orange dot marks the initial point near x=-11, y=1.15; a thick orange arrow follows the curve down to a green square marker at the first local minimum near x=-9.6, y=-8.11. A purple rounded label reads 'Reach Local Minima' with a purple pointer toward the green square.
Small parameter box with two columns and three rows: step | 0.1; initial x | -11; delta x | 0.1.
Formula displayed as a fraction: numerator x^2 cos(x) - x, denominator 10, with f(x) on the left.
Two annotation lines: 'X is in between -9.7 and color red bold -9.6' and 'f(x) is in between -8.08 and -8.011'. The second line literally shows -8.011 even though the table cell shows -8.11.
Red block arrow from the parameter box pointing right/down toward the table.

imagery: No photos or external icons; the only illustration is the vector-style function plot described above.
typography_notes: Sans-serif throughout, likely Arial/Calibri. Title is large bold red; subtitle is bold blue with 'initial point' in red and 'learning rate' in blue. Table text is small and dense; row labels are plain, numerals are compact. The formula uses italic math variables. No all-caps text except none; no numbered bullets.
animation_state: Static slide; no mid-build indicators. All table rows, the plot, and all callouts are fully visible.
recreation_brief: 1) Use a 16:9 light-gray slide and add a white content rectangle with a thick purple border. 2) Place the title 'Non-Convex Function' top-left in large bold red. 3) Below it, add the subtitle in bold blue: 'May reach different minimum value based on:' then a second line 'initial point and learning rate', making 'initial point' red and 'learning rate' blue. 4) Add a yellow circle at the top-right with black text '33'. 5) Add the small parameter box at the left-middle with rows step | 0.1, initial x | -11, delta x | 0.1, and a red block arrow pointing toward the table. 6) Add the formula f(x) = (x^2 cos(x) - x) / 10 in the center as a fraction. 7) Add the annotation lines exactly: 'X is in between -9.7 and color red bold -9.6' and 'f(x) is in between -8.08 and -8.011'. 8) Insert the bottom table with one label column and 16 data columns using the exact rows listed in visual_elements[0]; keep the text small and dense. 9) Color the table rows in alternating pale green/blue/purple/pink bands, and highlight the local-minimum columns; make x=-9.6 and f(x)=-8.11 red/bold. 10) Draw the top-right plot with black axes, light gridlines, x ticks -12 to -2 and y ticks 0 to -10, a green oscillating curve, a red initial dot near (-11, 1.15), an orange arrow to a green square at the first local minimum, and a purple 'Reach Local Minima' callout pointing to that square.
